problems.source_says: The main text never says which Experiment 2B ideas the newness analysis compares, or how the analysis is run. The experts classified every response, and in Experiment 2B 'responses' include the 100 unedited ChatGPT-only outputs that no participant wrote. If 'ChatGPT' in the result sentence means those outputs, the form-spec codes are question none, AI availability mixed and comparison ai_vs_human, as in S3-O4. The text names no comparison group, so 'Human-only' is a guess. It gives no analysis unit either, and 'output' differs from the participant unit the form gives the other ChatGPT-assisted versus Human-only outcomes (S3-O1, S3-O2). The direction 'mixed' rests on the same unnamed comparison: 'less effective at generating radically new ideas', like the abstract's 'most effective at generating incrementally (versus radically) new ideas', can compare ChatGPT's two kinds of ideas with each other, not with a control arm. The form marks the arms unresolved but still codes every field that depends on them. Fix: move the result to notes until Supplementary Note G names the arms and the analysis.
problems.quote: We tested this hypothesis by classifying the type of creativity featured in each response (incrementally new versus radically new versus not new).
problems.locator: PDF p. 3 (journal p. 1908), Results, Experiment 2B, first paragraph, and paragraph beginning 'We also examined the type of creativity'; PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1912), Methods, Experiment 2B, 'Creativity ratings'; PDF p. 1, abstract

problems.source_says: The Experiment 2B tests are contrasts in one model over 300 ideas: 200 participant ideas and 100 ChatGPT-only responses with no participant (F2,297 and t297, that is 300 minus 3 groups). The form-spec says the unit is the unit of the paper's own analysis, and output when the model has one row per idea. In Experiments 2A, 3, 4 and 5 every row is one participant's single idea, so participant fits there. In 2B a third of the rows belong to no participant. The form itself codes this same model as unit output, n_units 300, in S3-O4 and S3-O5. The printed effect sizes also carry the three-group error variance. With arms of about 100 (arm ns are not printed), 13.30 x sqrt(1/100 + 1/100) = 1.88 and 12.54 x sqrt(1/100 + 1/100) = 1.77, the printed d values. The two participant arms' own pooled s.d., sqrt((0.47^2 + 0.89^2)/2) = 0.71, would give a lay-judge d of about 1.66. Coded participant, these records would enter pooling (codebook sections 9 and 10) as participant-level effects, which they are not. Fix: unit output, n_units 300, as one screener coded.

problems.form_value: 'ChatGPT-assisted (both constraint levels; 2 x 2 ANOVA main effect)' versus 'Web-search-assisted (both constraint levels)'; the same with both empathy levels
problems.source_says: Each printed 'main effect' equals one simple effect, so it does not pool both levels. Experiment 4: sqrt(5.06) = 2.25, and P = 0.025, the same as the High-constraint t396 = 2.25, P = 0.025. Experiment 5: sqrt(49.26) = 7.02, and P = 1.04 × 10−11, the same as the Baseline-empathy t379 = 7.02, P = 1.04 × 10−11. With about 100 people per cell, a main effect over both levels would give about F = 10.8 (Experiment 4) and F = 75.4 (Experiment 5). So contrast 3 repeats S5-O1 contrast 1 and S6-O1 contrast 2, and a separate both-level contrast counts those cells twice. The form's open_questions raises this and calls it unresolved, but the printed numbers settle it. Fix: label the contrast as the paper's 'main effect' that equals the High-constraint (Experiment 4) or Baseline-empathy (Experiment 5) simple effect, or drop it.

problems.form_value: Not coded as an outcome. S1-O1 measure_detail mentions it, and the notes say it is reported only in Supplementary Note F.
problems.source_says: The main text reports this result's direction: the ChatGPT-assisted condition had a higher share of ideas with top-ranked creativity scores than the Web-search-assisted condition. It is a with_ai result scored on the output (lay-judge creativity), so the notes' reason for leaving it out is wrong. The form codes S3-O3 from the same kind of evidence, a direction-only sentence that points to a Supplementary Note, so the two results are treated differently. This is minor: S1-O1 stays the primary record. Fix: code it (direction treatment_higher, statistics_available none) or correct the notes.

confirmed: Every outcome is scored on the ideas: by lay judges (S1-O1, S1-O3, S1-O4, S2-O1, S3-O1, S3-O4, S4-O1, S4-O2, S5-O1, S6-O1), by three expert judges (S1-O2, S2-O2, S3-O2, S3-O3, S3-O5, S5-O2, S6-O2), or as a count of ideas entered (S1-O5). None is self-reported (PDF p. 2, paragraph before Results; PDF pp. 6-8, Methods, 'Creativity ratings' for each experiment).

The self-reports are correctly left out: the Experiment 3 idea exposition aid, the other Supplementary Note I items and PANAS, and the Experiment 2B self-reported modification (r = 0.11, P = 0.291) (PDF pp. 3-4, Results, Experiment 3; PDF p. 7, Methods, 'Process measures'; PDF p. 3, Experiment 2B, 'In sum' paragraph).

ChatGPT was available while every ChatGPT-assisted idea was written: participants were instructed to use ChatGPT (Experiments 1, 2B, 3), told they could use the ChatGPT website (2A), or assigned to the ChatGPT-assisted condition (4, 5). So ai_available_when_produced 'yes', timing 'immediate' and question 'with_ai' hold for the 15 with_ai outcomes whose arms are named (PDF p. 2, Experiments 1 and 2A; PDF p. 3, Experiments 2B and 3; PDF p. 4, Experiment 4; PDF p. 5, Experiment 5; PDF p. 7, Methods, Experiment 2B).

No outcome compares the similarity or diversity of different people's ideas, and no idea is produced after AI is removed, so no across_people or after_ai record is missing and no diversity or flexibility construct is needed (PDF pp. 1-9, main text and Methods; PDF pp. 10-12, Reporting Summary).

S3-O4 and S3-O5 compare 100 unedited GPT-3.5 responses with human ideas, so question 'none' and ai_available 'mixed' follow the form-spec field note on 'question' (PDF p. 7, Methods, Experiment 2B; form-spec, Field notes, 'question').

Constructs and measures fit the codebook: the six-item lay score and the two-item expert score are overall_creativity (human_raters, expert_raters); the originality items (original/innovative/creative) are novelty; the appropriateness items (practical/effective/useful) are usefulness; the number of ideas is fluency with category_count; the five-item articulateness rating is other (PDF p. 6, Methods, Experiment 1, 'Creativity ratings'; PDF p. 7, 'Process measures').

Unit 'participant' is the paper's own unit in Experiments 1, 2A, 3, 4 and 5: Experiment 1 averages each participant's idea scores, and the t-test degrees of freedom equal people analyzed minus cells (231 = 233 - 2, 288 = 291 - 3, 192 = 194 - 2, 396 = 400 - 4, 379 = 383 - 4), for lay and expert judges alike (PDF p. 6, Methods, Experiment 1, 'Creativity ratings'; PDF pp. 2-5, Results; Table 1, PDF p. 5).

Every 'reported' string matches the PDF text and Table 1 digit for digit, including the Experiment 2B ChatGPT-only s.d. (0.40 in Table 1 and the first sentence, 0.30 in the ChatGPT-assisted versus ChatGPT-only sentence) and the repeated 'ChatGPT-assisted × Low constraints' row label in Table 1 (PDF pp. 2-5, Results; Table 1, PDF p. 5; PDF p. 6, Methods, Experiment 1, number of ideas).

The Fig. 1 total effect (c: beta = 0.24, Z = 2.58, P = 0.010, 95% CI (0.06, 0.43)) and the articulateness contrast (t192 = 3.86, d = 0.55) match S4-O1 and S4-O2 (PDF p. 4, Fig. 1 and Results, Experiment 3).

Directions match the text wherever the arms are named, including no_clear_difference for the Experiment 2A expert contrast with Human-only (t288 = 1.79, P = 0.075, Bayes factor 0.71) and for the number of ideas (t231 = 1.42) (PDF p. 2, Experiment 2A; PDF p. 6, Methods, Experiment 1).

Comparison types with named arms follow codebook section 5: Google search without AI chatbot functions is ai_vs_active, and Human-only (no aid, no external websites) is ai_vs_bau (PDF p. 2, Experiment 1, definition of 'Web search'; PDF p. 2, Experiment 2A; PDF p. 7, Methods, Experiment 2B).

The expert contrasts in Experiments 4 and 5 pool the second factor, as measure_detail says: their 95% CIs, (0.15, 0.55) and (0.58, 1.00), are about 1/sqrt(2) as wide as the simple-effect CIs, which fits twice the number of people per arm (PDF p. 4, Experiment 4; PDF p. 5, Experiment 5).
summary: Every outcome is scored on the ideas, the constructs and measures fit the codebook, the units match the paper's analysis in Experiments 1, 2A, 3, 4 and 5, and every reported number matches the PDF exactly. The coding is still refuted on four points: S3-O3's arm-dependent codes have no support in the text, S3-O1 and S3-O2 are coded participant although the paper's model counts 300 ideas (100 with no participant), the two 2 x 2 'main effect' contrasts each repeat one simple effect, and the form leaves out the Experiment 1 top-ranked-idea result that the main text reports.
